episode.title: HPR4743: wl-copy
episode.author: Klaatu
episode.summary:
wl-copy is a command in the wl-clipboard package, and allows you to copy and paste data from your Linux Terminal on a Wayland desktop.
Copy an arbitrary string to your clipboard using wl-copy:

$ wl-copy "hello world"
Paste it anywhere on your system as usual (with Ctrl+Shift+V or a right-click and Paste).
You can copy from output, too:

$ echo "hello wide world" | wl-copy
You can redirect to wl-copy:

$ echo "hello world" &gt; example.txt

$ wl-copy &lt; ex

Pass OTP example.com pipe wl-copy. It does everything all in one.
You can copy a jpeg image. So wl-copy redirect, you know, less than symbol, example.jpeg.
WL copy is just sort of building upon what already has existed with an application called XClip.

notes.summary: This episode explains how to use the wl-copy command on a Wayland Linux desktop to copy text and data from the terminal to the system clipboard without using a mouse. It covers installation, basic usage with strings and command output, copying file contents, and alternatives like xclip for X11 systems. Listeners who work in terminals and want efficient copy-paste workflows will find this useful.
